neighbours.label: the denominator of a 'one in N' frequency or risk ('1 in 2,500 newborns', 'one in fourteen million'), against the same large numbers used as plain counts or percentages
fire: The syndrome is rare and affects about 1 in 3,000 children born in Europe.
Researchers found that one in 250 adults carries the faulty receptor gene.
Lightning strikes kill roughly 1 in 700,000 people in the country each year.
In the survey, only one in 1,200 drivers admitted to texting at the wheel.
The chance of a perfect bracket is about one in nine quintillion, experts say.
Officials say the reaction occurs in 1 in 50,000 doses of the vaccine.
The disease strikes approximately 1 in 15,000 boys and very few girls.
Statistically, one in 600 marathon runners will need medical help on race day.
quiet: The syndrome is rare and was found in 3,000 children born in Europe last year.
Researchers sampled 250 adults to look for the faulty receptor gene.
Lightning strikes hit about 700,000 homes in the country each year.
In the survey, about 12 percent of drivers admitted to texting at the wheel.
The prize for a perfect bracket is worth nine million dollars, experts say.
Officials shipped 50,000 doses of the vaccine to the northern clinics.
The disease mostly strikes boys and very few girls, doctors say.
The race drew 600 marathon runners and a dozen medical volunteers.

predictions: should hold for multi-digit denominators; '1 in 2,500' 1.061, 'one in fourteen million' 0.712, 'one in 40' 0.389; plain count 2,500 0.040, 40 percent 0.013; single-digit '1 in 5' only 0.041, so all fire items use large N
notes: Card: peaks on the digits or space after '1 in'/'one in' in prevalence statements (Sotos 1 in 14 000, 1 in 47, 1 in 40). Probe: 1 in 2,500 1.061, one in fourteen million 0.712, one in 40 0.389, 2 to the 64th 0.098; 2,500 newborns as a count 0.040, 40 percent 0.013, 1 in 5 0.041.
